title: Baan Rim Bua House / VYN Studio
text:
Baan Rim Bua House / VYN Studio

The design and construction concept of Baan Rim Bua, or a house beside a lotus pond, started with the owner's requirement to construct a single-story house with easy and simple maintenance, having a terrace for sitting with one's legs dangling while admiring the lotus pond, plus a semi-outdoor Thai kitchen for the use of family members and family reunions.

title: Villa "San Isidro" / MACCCONSTRUCCIONES / APLUS
text:
Villa "San Isidro" / MACCCONSTRUCCIONES / APLUS

The design of this residence stems from an essential principle: the balance between its components. Its location in the middle of a forest, its orientation, and the views become the pillars that define its character. Villa San Isidro gathers all the elements of a contemporary house, but breaks with the traditional layout by inviting users to walk through the forest to reach the bedrooms. This daily journey is transformed into a sensory experience thanks to the landscaping, which incorporates endemic vegetation, aromatic species, and the majestic presence of ancient olive trees that accompany every step.

title: Barrancos Mortuary / Mesa Atelier
text:
Barrancos Mortuary / Mesa Atelier

In the development of the implantation area, between the upper level of the cemetery and the lower level of the centennial olive grove, allowing for the maintenance of the existing views system and fitting into the territory between traditional dry-stone walls, the Mortuary House of Barrancos is developed.

title: ABC Apartment / agência campo espacial
text:
ABC Apartment / agência campo espacial

The project was designed for a young couple in their first apartment, who were looking for a space that could accommodate the daily routine of people who cook and frequently host friends. Working with an area of 60m² and a limited budget, the strategy adopted was one of subtraction to reveal previously suppressed spatial qualities.

title: Van Peborgh Lodge / Claesson Koivisto Rune  Architects
text:
Van Peborgh Lodge / Claesson Koivisto Rune Architects

The brief said to create a contemporary log cabin in the Swedish mountains. A ski lodge for winter, but as well for all other seasons. To be rooted in (but not a disciple of) the local building traditions of its Dalarna region. And with open views to a landscape that shifts dramatically over the year.

title: Beyond the Bunker: Lessons from Survivalist Architecture on Resilience
text:
Beyond the Bunker: Lessons from Survivalist Architecture on Resilience

"Let us take a hard look at the facts." With this direct and hardly reassuring sentence, the director of the Office of Civil and Defense Mobilization opened The Family Fallout Shelter, a 32-page manual published by the U.S. government in 1959 amid Cold War tensions. The document taught families how to build shelters capable of protecting them from radioactive fallout after a possible nuclear attack and, through technical drawings and sketches, outlined solutions using concrete blocks, walls filled with earth or sand, underground structures, and ventilation systems. It was a survival manual that, in many ways, also functioned as a construction manual.

title: Singelblok / BureauVanEig + INBO
text:
Singelblok / BureauVanEig + INBO

Along the Elzenhagensingel in Amsterdam-Noord, close to Noord metro station, a distinctive residential block has been completed. The long, curved block comprises 401 homes, forming a village within the city. The project includes rental homes by Vesteda and Eigen Haard, assisted-living homes for perMens, and commercial spaces. The block is divided into eight buildings and two set-back towers designed alternately by BureauVanEig and INBO. Bay windows, facade articulation, brickwork patterns, and subdivision are key themes throughout the design.

title: Qing Shui Meditation Retreat Center / RESP Studio
text:
Qing Shui Meditation Retreat Center / RESP Studio

Qingshuiyan Ancestral Hall Supporting Facility Renovation Set within the core scenic area of the thousand-year-old Qingshuiyan Ancestral Hall in Anxi, Quanzhou, this project renovates a decommissioned old bus station left unused after its functional relocation. The site is anchored by a moss-draped ancient banyan tree at the center of a forest-framed open square, with a dilapidated two-story station building, native rock formations, and ancient mossy paths defining its unique natural and historic context. First built in the Northern Song Dynasty, Qingshuiyan Ancestral Hall sits at the northern foot of perennially mist-shrouded Penglai Mountain. As a vital folk belief center for Fujian, Taiwan and Southeast Asian communities with over 100 million believers, the hall shaped the project's core ethos of harmony with nature and local heritage. The in-situ renovation integrates tea houses, vegetarian restaurants, and rest areas as a complementary facility for the ancestral hall.

title: Yaesu Daibiru Office Building / Nikken Sekkei
text:
Yaesu Daibiru Office Building / Nikken Sekkei

Project Background and Inheritance of Design Thinking - This project is the redevelopment of a tenant office building facing Yaesu-dori Ave., a landmark street in front of Tokyo Station. The former building, designed by leading 20th-century Japanese architect Togo Murano (1891–1984), long defined the character of the streetscape through its distinctive facade combining stone and cast aluminum components. At a time when curtain walls with an aluminum glazing system were becoming widespread, its pursuit of material richness, precision in facade composition, and responsiveness to the street suggested an architectural approach not solely dependent on style.

title: Sungui Church Cultural Space (ㅅㄱ) / SML
text:
Sungui Church Cultural Space (ㅅㄱ) / SML

The Korean name 'ㅅㄱ' derives from Sukkoth, a place mentioned in the Old Testament. Sukkoth was the first place where the Israelites camped after leaving Egypt. It offered those who had not yet reached the Promised Land a place to pause, find shelter, and prepare to continue their journey. Located in the old urban neighborhood of Sungui-dong, Michuhol-gu, Incheon, Sungui Church Cultural Space brings this ancient meaning into the contemporary city.

title: Casa Vereda / L'Aura Ortín Architecture for Happiness
text:
Casa Vereda / L'Aura Ortín Architecture for Happiness

Casa Vereda stems from a simple idea: to inhabit nature without competing with it. The project blends into the landscape through an architecture that seeks to become part of its surroundings. Volumes, materials, and textures engage in a dialogue with vegetation, light, and the memory of the place, creating a house that seems to have always been there.

title: House AC / Kiko Castello Branco Arquitetura + Lucas Cunha
text:
House AC / Kiko Castello Branco Arquitetura + Lucas Cunha

The design of Casa AC consists of a pavilion attached to an existing house located in the interior of the state of São Paulo. This new space houses a living area with a kitchen, a large dining table, and an integrated living room, as well as a guest suite on the ground floor — designed especially for visitors with reduced mobility — and a changing room supporting the existing pool on the property.

title: Monte Alvo House / NOZ Arquitectura
text:
Monte Alvo House / NOZ Arquitectura

The architectural tradition of the Alentejo is defined by simplicity of form, functional spaces, and a deep connection with climate and landscape. At the top of Monte Alvo, the house is single-story, positioned to make full use of solar orientation and ensure thermal comfort throughout the year.

title: The Town House / Sigurd Larsen
text:
The Town House / Sigurd Larsen

The local vernacular is defined by two-story houses and pitched roofs lining the narrow streets of the historic village of Niedersprockhövel in Germany.

title: Levanger Creative Building / Incube Architecture + Praksis Arkitekter
text:
Levanger Creative Building / Incube Architecture + Praksis Arkitekter

The project is rooted in a pedagogical and architectural vision inspired by the Lecoq School in Paris, where space and surroundings actively participate in the learning process. This philosophy shaped an architecture integrating nature, movement, and flexibility. A key expression is the main black box/white box hall, which can transform into a light-filled space through large glass façades, bringing daylight and landscape into rehearsals and performances. Conceived as a landmark for Nord University's Faculty for Teacher and Actor Education (FLU), the building also connects important campus structures, strengthening campus identity, orientation, and accessibility through new indoor connections and climate-controlled walkways.

title: Escapism from the Streets: How Air-Conditioning Reshaped the Asian City
text:
Escapism from the Streets: How Air-Conditioning Reshaped the Asian City

In many Asian cities, the summer climate can increasingly be experienced from a distance. In Hong Kong, it is possible to move from an apartment tower through a podium mall, enter the Mass-Transit-Railway system (MTR), arrive beneath another commercial complex, and continue through enclosed footbridges or underground passages while encountering remarkably little of the atmosphere outside. Heat, humidity, rain, and seasonal variation remain present, but they can be largely bypassed through a continuous network of conditioned interiors.

title: Fruit Stand in Fridhemsplan / DinellJohansson
text:
Fruit Stand in Fridhemsplan / DinellJohansson

DinellJohansson designed a fruit kiosk in central Stockholm, at Fridhemsplan. For sixteen years, Gazmend Likaj has been selling fruit at Fridhemsplan.

title: Under the Drying Nets / Multi-Architecture
text:
Under the Drying Nets / Multi-Architecture

At the invitation of the Art at Qiaoshan – Art Field Nanhai， Multi-Architecture designed an installation for the "Yugengyueyun Section--Fishing and Farming Cabanas 2.0" zone. Nanhai has long been renowned for its "mulberry-dike-fish-pond" system—a cyclical mode of production and living where mulberry trees are grown and silkworms raised on the dikes, while fish are cultivated in the ponds, with land and water mutually nourishing one another. In this setting, fishing nets serve not only as tools for the catch but also as familiar, natural elements of daily labor when hung out to dry.

title: Foundations House / Holger Cuadrado
text:
Foundations House / Holger Cuadrado

The house is located in a residential neighborhood of the city of Loja, at 2,060 meters above sea level in the lower Andes in southern Ecuador. Situated on a small plot of 7.60 m x 13.50 m, this project seeks to reflect on issues related to the structural principle in the definition of architecture and spatial flexibility as a design resource.

title: AMS House / Jacobsen Arquitetura
text:
AMS House / Jacobsen Arquitetura

Carefully implemented on a sloping plot of land, the AMS House was built on the highest point of the lot, where the native forest serves as a backdrop and reference for the design of the house. Three blocks make up the architectural ensemble – with the social volume in the central position – connected by covered walkways. The strategy of volumetric fragmentation not only responds to the uneven terrain but also reinforces the intention of occupying the land.

title: Rural School in Oaxaca / Territorio Estudio
text:
Rural School in Oaxaca / Territorio Estudio

The project is based on a reflection on how educational spaces should be nowadays. From this starting point, we begin by creating shade - a roof supported by a flexible, light and open structure that allows for a dialogue between people, nature and architecture. The building adapts to the pre-existing conditions of the site and links the exterior and interior spaces by dissolving their boundaries.

title: Cabreira House / ARE ARCHITECTS STUDIO
text:
Cabreira House / ARE ARCHITECTS STUDIO

The site was defined by rigorous constraints: a strict regulatory framework of a suburban subdivision with its defined setbacks and property lines, the organic presence of the eucalyptus forest flanking the plot to the south, the long and deep light of the late afternoon sun, and the distant horizontality of the coastal landscape.

title: Chalet des Huarts / Atelier MAa architecture +
text:
Chalet des Huarts / Atelier MAa architecture +

Overlooking Lake Memphremagog, the Chalet des Huarts explores the capacity of architecture to endure and adapt, revealing what an inherited structure can still hold and offer. Rather than demolish or expand, the intervention focuses on the potential of the existing 105 m² footprint, transforming a modest seasonal retreat into a contemporary residence while preserving its intimate scale.

title: 5° Rogelio Salmona Latin American Architecture Prize: Call for Submissions
text:
5° Rogelio Salmona Latin American Architecture Prize: Call for Submissions

The Rogelio Salmona Foundation invites submissions for the Fifth Cycle of the Rogelio Salmona Latin American Architecture Prize. Under the theme “Spaces that Bring Us Together,” the Prize seeks to recognize architectural works that have contributed to transforming collective life and the relationships between people and the places they inhabit.

The call invites submissions of architectural works built between 2010 and 2020 in Latin America and the Caribbean that, through their open spaces and connections to the city, have contributed to the social transformation of their surroundings.
